newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht steady, liquidity improves.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht steady, liquidity improves.

text.p: * Thai baht relatively steady but still fragile in face of dollar's firm tone and continued bearish sentiment for Thailand.
* Malaysian ringgit firms, Singapore dollar weakens on back of early ringgit/Sing buying by U.S. funds but gains slowed by market holiday in Malaysia.
* Indonesian rupiah scarcely moves due to absence of Jakarta players for Eid al-Fitr holidays. Seen in 2,377.0-2,378.0 range against U.S. dollar.
The Thai baht remained relatively calm as Singapore players returned on Tuesday after a long weekend but failed to buy the dollar aggressively.
"The market was back to normal this morning after heavy buying of the dollar last week. There was also some selling interest in the dollar," said a senior dealer at a local bank in Bangkok.
The baht was quoted at 25.942/25.945 to the dollar at 0420 GMT compared with 25.935/25.950 late on Monday. The Bank of Thailand (BOT) fixed the mid-rate at 25.91 per dollar against 25.90 on Monday.
The baht has come under selling pressure over the past few weeks due to concern about the sluggish economy and a bearish stock market.

Dealers said the market had a muted response to reports that Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan had said the BOT might need to adjust the basket of currencies against which the baht is weighted in the face of the current baht weakness.
"They've been saying that for a long time but the underlying thing is they cannot change the basket till the baht stabilises," said a senior dealer at a Thai bank in Singapore.
The Thai overnight interbank rate fell to 14.00-16.00 percent in early trade against 18.00-20.00 late on Monday as funds flowed back to the market after Lunar New Year withdrawals, dealers said.
In Singapore, buying of the Malaysian ringgit/Singapore dollar cross dominated early trade, with Kuala Lumpur players still out for the Moslem New Year holiday.
A U.S. bank dealer said New York-based funds were seen buying the cross from an opening level of 0.5660/65, pushing dollar/ringgit to a low of 2.4825 and taking dollar/Sing towards a 1.4120 high.
"I think it was just people going into carry trades again because if you short dollars against the ringgit, you can make on the swap points," he said.
He said the original move seemed to be driven by funds establishing new positions but it had caused other players to follow suit.
Dealers said the ringgit/Sing cross would face strong resistance at the psychological and technical level of 0.5700. It was quoted at 0.5677/83 at 0420 GMT.
The Singapore dollar shrugged off weekend news of an upward revision in the city-state's 1996 Gross Domestic Product to 7.0 percent from a previous estimate of 6.5 percent.
Dealers said it was likely to trade between 1.4090 and 1.4150 against the U.S. dollar in the near term.
-- Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
